speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a history involving gait and limb ataxia; to understand the underlying cause, can you describe exactly how your walking and coordination have changed over time?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: You mentioned the symptoms are more pronounced on the right side; can you tell me if you have any weakness in your arms or legs, and do you experience any numbness or tingling?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is a very important detail; since you are taking natalizumab for Crohn's disease, have you noticed any recent changes in your bowel movements or any new neurological symptoms like vision problems or seizures?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had a recent fever or major infection that I know of. The symptoms are mostly gait imbalance, limb ataxia, and weaker use of my right arm.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast, focusing on the brainstem and cerebellum.
DIAGNOSIS READY: PML (Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy) secondary to natalizumab therapy.
